summary: Self-hosted runners failing git fetch after internal proxy TLS cert rotation (CA chain ordering)
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC we rotated the TLS certificate for proxy.internal.redwood.ai (used by self-hosted CI runners to access Git endpoints). After rotation many self-hosted runners reported failures when performing git fetch/clone against GitHub/GitLab through the proxy. Failures started immediately after the rotation and affected multiple release pipelines.

Impact:
- Intermittent to consistent git fetch failures on ~40% of self-hosted runners in us-west-2 for ~90 minutes.
- Several release jobs timed out and triggered retries; customer-facing deploys delayed.
- No effect on hosted API traffic or Dedicated GPU pools.

Environment:
- prod region: us-west-2
- affected runner group: self-hosted-release-runners (ephemeral Linux images, amd64)
- proxy: proxy.internal.redwood.ai (TLS termination for outbound git traffic)
- cert provisioning: cert-manager (internal ACME) backed by internal CA

Steps to reproduce (observed on an affected runner):
1. On runner: git fetch origin main --depth=1
2. Error: fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo.git/': SSL: certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)
3. Running curl -v https://proxy.internal.redwood.ai resulted in "SSL: certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate"
4. openssl s_client -connect proxy.internal.redwood.ai:443 -showcerts shows chain served but certificate order is intermediate-first (bad chain ordering)

Logs / snippets:
- Git error from runner: "fatal: unable to access 'https://...': SSL: certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)"
- curl output: "SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate"
- openssl s_client output excerpt: "Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=proxy.internal.redwood.ai
   i:/C=US/O=Redwood Internal CA/OU=Intermediate CA
 1 s:/C=US/O=Redwood Internal CA/OU=Intermediate CA
   i:/C=US/O=Redwood Root CA
WARNING: no safe protocol available"

Immediate actions taken:
- Support paged SRE on call and pinned incident to P1. (see #sre on Slack)
comments: 2026-03-12 03:05 UTC - Ravi Patel: Acknowledged. I can reproduce SSL verify errors on an ephemeral runner in us-west-2. Opening tcpdump + openssl to inspect cert chain.

2026-03-12 03:28 UTC - SRE Oncall (Ana Gomez): Found the proxy serving a certificate chain where the intermediate and end-entity certs are sent in the wrong order. Some client stacks (the runner base image) treat this as an untrusted chain.

2026-03-12 04:02 UTC - Maya Chen: Rolled back the partial proxy rollout from canary edge (instances 3/10 had the new configuration). After rollback, affected runners recovered within ~10 minutes. Recording as workaround while we investigate root cause.

2026-03-12 08:45 UTC - Infra (Jordan Lee): Root cause: cert-manager issued a new cert bundle but our deployment script used concatenation order (intermediate + leaf) instead of (leaf + intermediate). The change was introduced in infra PR 4827. Patch submitted to ensure fullchain ordering and add a validation step.
2026-03-13 11:20 UTC - Security (Priya Nair): Confirmed no private keys were exposed and CA hierarchy is intact. Adding additional gate for cert rotations in the pipeline.

2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - Ravi Patel: Re-deployed corrected proxy config with fullchain in correct order and added preflight tests. Monitoring for 24 hours. Marking investigation as complete; follow-ups scheduled.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC: cert-manager rotated proxy cert via automated pipeline (infra PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4827).
- 02:05 UTC: first runner failure observed (git fetch SSL verify error).
- 02:30 UTC: SRE identified wrong certificate chain order served by proxy (intermediate sent before leaf).
- 03:50 UTC: partial rollback of proxy config to pre-rotation version performed; runner failures decreased.
- Root cause: packaging step in rollout pipeline concatenated certs in wrong order when constructing tls.crt for proxy. Some client TLS stacks tolerate chain order differences; our ephemeral runner images (older ca-certificates + OpenSSL build) do not and fail verification.
- Additional contributing factor: rollout pipeline did not include a post-deploy TLS client validation check against an ephemeral runner image.

Evidence collected:
- openssl s_client output and captured pcap showing TLS handshake failures on affected runners.
- infra PR 4827 amended cert concat order; unit test did not catch chain ordering because unit tests validated presence of certs but not ordering.

Hypotheses tested:
- Bad SANs or missing intermediate -> rejected: intermediate present but ordering wrong.
- CA rotation mismatch in runner image -> rejected: adding the correct fullchain served by proxy resolves errors on same runner image.
resolution:
Short-term fix: Rolled back the proxy change to the previous cert bundle (03:50 UTC) and then deployed a corrected fullchain order (leaf + intermediate + root) with a canary and quick validation. Affected runners recovered within ~10 minutes after corrected deployment.

Permanent fix implemented:
- Infra PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4827 fixes cert concat order and adds an integration test that validates chain ordering by running openssl s_client against a canary runner image.
- Added a preflight TLS validation step in the proxy rollout job that performs a git fetch against a bootstrap runner image.
- Added alerting rule when >5% of runner git fetches in a 5m window fail with SSL verify errors (channel: #sre-alerts).

No data leakage or private key exposure found. No customer data impacted beyond delayed deploys.
follow_up_actions: Create a short runbook for TLS cert rotation that includes chain-order validation and a canary validation step (owner: Infra)
Backfill integration test to run against the oldest supported runner image to catch compatibility regressions (owner: CI-Team)
Add automated certificate chain ordering check to cert-manager provisioning pipeline (owner: Security)
Schedule post-incident review with Infra and SRE to discuss rollout gating (calendar invite: /events/INC-67901-PIR)
